# Example transcript: running s05.
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture. The INSPECT-mode output
# (the assembled prompt) IS deterministic and is what the tests pin; the RUN-mode
# reply from a live LLM is non-deterministic, so for that part what matters is
# the SHAPE: the model replies in the format the prompt requested.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. List the formats that have a prompt set. No network, no API key.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -list
Known edit formats (each has its own prompt set):
  diff   SEARCH/REPLACE blocks (s03, aider default)
  udiff  unified diff hunks (s04)
  whole  return the entire updated file (s02)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. INSPECT the SEARCH/REPLACE (diff) system prompt — this is the string that
#    makes s03's parser have anything to parse. Note: {fence[0]} rendered to
#    ```, and {final_reminders} rendered to the "lazy" nudge.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -format diff
===== SYSTEM PROMPT (format=diff) =====
Act as an expert software developer.
Always use best practices when coding.
Respect and use existing conventions, libraries, etc that are already present in the code base.
You are diligent and tireless!
You NEVER leave comments describing code without implementing it!
You always COMPLETELY IMPLEMENT the needed code!

Take requests for changes to the supplied code.
...
# *SEARCH/REPLACE block* Rules:
...
2. The opening fence and code language, eg: ```python
3. The start of search block: <<<<<<< SEARCH
...
7. The end of the replace block: >>>>>>> REPLACE
8. The closing fence: ```
...

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. INSPECT the whole-file prompt + its few-shot examples. The wholefile prompt
#    has NO SEARCH/REPLACE markers — a different format means a different prompt,
#    selected by the SAME renderer. The literal `{name}` in the example code
#    survives substitution (it is NOT a placeholder).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -format whole -examples
===== SYSTEM PROMPT (format=whole) =====
Act as an expert software developer.
...
To suggest changes to a file you MUST return the entire content of the updated file.
...

===== FEW-SHOT EXAMPLE MESSAGES (format=whole) =====

--- USER ---
Change the greeting to be more casual

--- ASSISTANT ---
Ok, I will:

1. Switch the greeting text from "Hello" to "Hey".

show_greeting.py
```
import sys

def greeting(name):
    print(f"Hey {name}")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    greeting(sys.argv[1])
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. RUN mode: render the diff prompt and actually call the model once. The
#    prompt + few-shot examples steer the model to reply with SEARCH/REPLACE
#    blocks; you'd then feed that reply to s03's GetEdits to apply it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
$ go run . -v -format diff -file greet.go -instruction "change the greeting to 'hi there'"

# --- stderr (the -v trace) ---
[s05] format=diff provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-4-6
[s05] system prompt: 1583 bytes, 2 few-shot turns
[s05] stop_reason=end_turn in=712 out=58 tokens

# --- stdout (the model's reply, in the requested format) ---
greet.go
```go
<<<<<<< SEARCH
	return "hello"
=======
	return "hi there"
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

# --- stderr footer ---
[s05] ^ the model replied in the format the prompt requested; feed this to the
      matching s02/s03/s04 parser to apply it.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Switch the format flag to whole, same file/instruction — and the model now
#    replies with a full file listing instead, because the SELECTED prompt
#    changed. The loop code did not.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -format whole -file greet.go -instruction "change the greeting to 'hi there'"
greet.go
```
package main

import "fmt"

func greet() string {
	return "hi there"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(greet())
}
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The deterministic tests (these DO run in CI, no network):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test ./...
ok  	learn-aider/s05	0.5s
